paragraphs.text: Hoxha-Aliu syndrome (HXAL) is an autosomal recessive disorder caused by biallelic null variants in the ERI1 gene. Its main features are mild intellectual disability and anomalies of the hands and feet, including brachydactyly, clinodactyly, short metacarpals, dysplastic nails, and toe syndactyly (Hoxha and Aliu, 2023; Guo et al., 2023).

paragraphs.text: Szot et al. (2021) reported a girl (F5.II.1) who had microcephaly, global developmental delay, and autism. Her other features included brachycephaly, a flat occiput, bitemporal narrowing, and cupped, prominent ears. She had limb reduction defects: a transverse terminal limb reduction of the right hand with a rudimentary fifth digit, hypoplastic deep-set nails, absent toes, absent nails on the toes, and syndactyly. She also had a perimembranous ventricular septal defect, pulmonary vein stenosis, and bilateral inguinal hernias. In addition to the ERI1 variant (see MOLECULAR GENETICS), she carried a homozygous missense variant in the KYNU gene.

paragraphs.text: Szot et al. (2021) performed trio exome or genome sequencing in a girl (F5.II.1) who had limb reduction defects, cardiac anomalies, microcephaly, and developmental delay. She was homozygous for a loss-of-function variant in the ERI1 gene, c.514C-T (NM_153332.4), which results in a gln172-to-ter (Q172X) substitution. She was also homozygous for a missense variant in the KYNU gene. The authors noted that her limb and cardiac abnormalities resembled those of the patient with a homozygous ERI1-MFHAS1 microdeletion reported by Choucair et al. (2017). They also stated that the functional link between ERI1 mutation and these defects remained to be assessed.

paragraphs.text: Guo et al. (2023) described 2 distinct phenotypes caused by biallelic ERI1 variants. Five affected individuals with missense variants had severe spondyloepimetaphyseal dysplasia (SEMD). Individuals with biallelic null variants did not have SEMD; they had mild intellectual disability and digital anomalies. The missense variants caused loss of exoribonuclease activity, which led to defective trimming of the 5.8S rRNA 3-prime end and decreased degradation of replication-dependent histone mRNAs. Induced pluripotent stem cells derived from affected individuals showed impaired in vitro chondrogenesis, with downregulation of genes that regulate skeletal patterning. The authors concluded that, within recessive genotypes, the missense alleles had a more severe effect than the null alleles.

She had microcephaly, global developmental delay, autism, limb reduction defects, a ventricular septal defect, pulmonary vein stenosis, and bilateral inguinal hernias.
